description: This sprint's own design decisions section states the extraction of note_browser_common.select_paid_price() was done 'so BOTH that script [note-set-single-price.py] ... and lib/note-publish-live.py ... share the exact SAME selection sequence rather than one re-inventing it,' and both note-publish-live.py's and note-set-single-price.py's docstrings assert 'Moving this here changes nothing observable about note-set-single-price.py's own stdout/behavior.' That claim has NO live/E2E regression test backing it for note-set-single-price.py, the refactor's ORIGINAL caller. tests/test-prop21-visual-and-single-price.sh (which is this sprint's only test touching note-set-single-price.py) is explicitly a 'structural/static oracle (grep + python3 -m py_compile)' per its own header comment -- it never executes the script against a real or stubbed browser session, and never asserts SINGLE_PRICE_TYPE/SINGLE_PRICE_VALUE/SINGLE_PRICE_PANEL_SCREENSHOT output post-refactor. The ONLY live proof that select_paid_price() still behaves correctly is test-prop22b-live-publish-real-click.sh's green-phase run -- but that exercises the function through the NEW caller, note-publish-live.py, not through note-set-single-price.py. A regression specific to note-set-single-price.py's call site (e.g. a difference in how its own control flow interacts with the shared function, or an accidental change to the panel-screenshot-before-cancel sequence documented as CRIT-105's own required artifact) would go completely undetected by this sprint's test suite.
